
=================================================================
#46 Gyeol (結)  (647 January)
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: surabol · tone: political thriller — countdown
Logline: Yushin asks the water who he is. Then the gate opens from the inside, the yard’s two best meet between the camps, and the score finally breaks.
=================================================================
[0] ══ DAY: DAY 9 ══
[1] ¶ The water under the hill has been warm for thirty years. Before light on the ninth day, so is the stone in Yushin’s sleeve.
[2] ── SCENE: The Lake, Again ──
[3] ¶ So Yushin goes to the cavern lake, as if habit could hold a country together.
[4] ¶ Yushin undresses without ceremony. The three are already in the steam — mentors, tormentors, the only room in Silla where no one asks him for a victory.
[5] ¶ Golhwa knows that walk and is already wet for it. She watches him like a problem she means to solve with her body.
[6] Golhwa: You came early. How flattering.
[7] Narim: He came because he is about to kill a friend. / Forest etiquette: say it plain.
[8] Kim Yushin: If you know that, tell me how not to.
[9] Hyullé: You can’t. / …I’m sorry. / Keep the wound that remembers the headband. Lose the one that wants him to thank you for the blade.
[10] Golhwa: Unless you’re saving all your thank-yous for the Queen again. / She is not in the water, Yushin. We are.
[11] ¶ She takes his wrist under the water and does not wait for the Queen’s name to finish. For a few breaths there is only steam, and the walk they already know, and a marshal who cannot keep his arithmetic. Then Narim’s voice cuts the wick.
[12] Kim Yushin: But Her Majesty —
[13] Narim: Enough, fire. / He will go. We knew that when he took the armour off and still kept her name on.
[14] Hyullé: …Go. / Give Sunduk the victory. / Keep a little silence for us.
[15] Narim: So the stone woke you. / One question, Kim. From the water. Once.
[16] ¶ Steam thins. Two shapes wait where the rock shelves into black: the father who taught him that loyalty is soil, and the grandfather who traded a kingdom so a grandson could keep a sword.
[17] Kim Yushin: Father. Grandfather. / In eight days the same mouth has called me the sacred country’s saviour and a Gaya wretch. / Which of the two do I carry out to the tenth morning?
[18] Kim Seohyun: Yushin, my beloved son. / You were the light of my life, and now the nation needs you to be its savior. / I am sorry that I was not of Silla blood… I tried my hardest to forget my Gaya roots, and tried to pretend that I was something I was not. / But you don’t need to do that anymore. / Son, you are the mighty Sword of Silla, and the Last Prince of Gaya. / But you are infinitely more than that…! / You are my son. You are Kim Yushin. / Your mother and I couldn’t be more proud of you…!
[19] Kim Muryuk: Yushin, my beloved grandson. / When I swore allegiance to the Silla crown, it was not for my own sake, but for yours. / I loved you before I knew you. / Yushin, look at me. / I am so, so proud of you…!
[20] Kim Yushin: Father… / Grandfather… / Thank you.
[21] Golhwa: Look at him — he’s crying.
[22] ¶ He comes up out of the water with the stone gone cold again in his fist. He does not need it warm any more.
[23] ── SCENE: The Outer Works ──
[24] ¶ By midday the ninth day has turned into the battle both sides spent eight days pretending they could avoid. Assault and counter-assault in the outer works.
[25] ¶ Yumjong goes down in the outer ditch with a Silla spear under his arm. Bidam reaches him before the rebels finish falling back.
[26] [battle]
[27] Yumjong: Don’t— don’t make that face, Councillor. / They marched. You said they wouldn’t. They marched… / …It was a good word, though. Gaya. They liked shouting it.
[28] Bidam: Yumjong. / …Yumjong.
[29] ¶ The quieter name on the banner goes first. Bidam closes his eyes for him and does not let anyone see his hand.
[30] ¶ By dusk the granary inside the Moon Palace is down to its last sacks, and men who have never prayed are learning the postures. Alchun is asked, for the last useful time, which wall he belongs to.
[31] Alchun: I belong to the country that survives the week. / If that answer is empty — then so is the chair you will offer me afterward.
[32] ¶ He still does not draw. Surabol will remember that sentence for years: the man who caught tigers, filed under Neither.
[33] ── SCENE: The Rampart ──
[34] ¶ That night, on Radiance’s rampart, Bidam speaks — to his officers, to the wall, to whichever chronicler is still awake. They expect a battle plan. They get a confession.
[35] Bidam: You know… we call this country the “sacred country.” But our country isn’t the greatest in the world. / Its kings are not the most wise. Its armies are not the strongest. / Its men are not the most noble. Its women are not the most chaste. / Our natural scenery is beautiful, but there are more beautiful sights elsewhere. / For every good thing our nation has, there are other nations with greater things.
[36] Bidam: However — that is not why we call it the sacred country.
[37] Bidam: We call it the sacred country, because it is ours. / Because our kings rule over our people. Because our armies are composed of our sons. / Because our men get up every day, and try to make the next day better. / Because our women go to sleep every night, knowing that they have raised our next generation with our blood and our seed. / Because our hills and rivers are the ones that we have grown up with as children — where we used to play with our fathers, and where we will play with our sons.
[38] Bidam: That is what I am defending.
[39] Bidam: The crown may call me a traitor, a heretic, an old man who needs to adapt to the times… / …and to all of that, I simply say no. / I don’t need to say any more than that.
[40] Bidam: And one day, our descendants will prove me right. / So come at me, fate! **Bidam is ready to defend what is ours.**
[41] ══ DAY: DAY 10 ══
[42] ¶ Before the gate opens Bidam goes down to the lines and saddles **Bisamun** himself, which a High Councillor does not do. He slips nine beads off the end of his string and knots them to the bridle, under the horse’s jaw.
[43] ?: Sangdaedeung, those are…
[44] Bidam: Master Wongwang’s fifth precept. Be choosy about killing. / Never the animals that work for you. Horse, ox, chicken, dog. / …They burned a white horse over there two nights ago. Even if I lose, somebody should still be holding on to this one.
[45] ¶ Bisamun is named for the guardian king who stands at the north of every temple with a pagoda in his hand. Bidam rubs the horse’s nose once and speaks to it in the voice he keeps for sutras.
[46] Bidam: You’re named for the one who guards the north. / Today just watch the west.
[47] ❝QUOTE (Diamond Sutra (金剛般若波羅蜜經) §32, tr. Kumārajīva · T08n0235, p. 752b · Sanskrit: Vajracchedikā §32 (Conze ed.)) [Bidam]: All conditioned things are like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, a shadow; like dew, and like lightning. So should you see them.❞
[48] ── SCENE: Between the Camps ──
[49] ¶ On the tenth morning the grain is gone, and the palace gate opens from the inside, exactly as Bidam said it would. Out of it comes the Marshal of Silla at a gallop, on a grey horse that had no name the day before yesterday.
[50] ¶ Bidam rides out to meet him and stops halfway. He gets down, slaps Bisamun on the rump and sends him back to the lines. A spear’s length off, Yushin gets down too. They learned this on foot.
[51] ¶ They meet again between the camps — not as High Councillor and marshal, but as the yard’s two best. Dragon pommel against heavenly horse. The first exchanges are almost gentle. That is how Hwarang kill each other.
[52] ¶ The yard drill first. High guard, cut, step, return. Bidam is fifty-three and moves like it, until he doesn’t.
[53] Bidam: You still drop your left shoulder.
[54] Kim Yushin: You still talk.
[55] ¶ Bidam’s third cut is a feint and the fourth isn’t. It opens a line above Yushin’s brow, right where a Hwarang headband sits. Yushin’s hand goes to his forehead, the way a new boy’s does in the hall when the seniors start in on him.
[56] ¶ Yushin steps inside the next cut, too close for either blade. Bidam’s bead string catches on the dragon ring of his hilt. For one breath they are tied together at the wrist.
[57] Bidam: …Let go, Gaya.
[58] Kim Yushin: You let go.
[59] ¶ Neither does. The string does instead.
[60] ¶ Yushin wins the way a man wins when he would rather lose — late, ugly, through a guard he taught Bidam twenty years ago. The heavenly-horse blade drops. Blood finds the mud that used to be a scoreboard.
[61] ¶ Ninety-nine beads go into the mud after the blood, one at a time, like somebody counting.
[62] Bidam: …One hundred and nine. / Finally.
[63] ¶ Bidam smiles with blood in his teeth — the same boy who once offered a headband across a desk.
[64] Bidam: Hwarang Kim Yushin…
[65] ¶ Yushin does not move to finish it, and there is nothing left to finish. For as long as the breath lasts the two of them look at each other the way they used to across the yard, back when the score was even and neither one wanted to go home.
[66] ¶ Kangrim reads his name three times where the body has not yet finished falling — Bidam. Bidam. Bidam. — the ledger catching up to the last word.
[67] Kangrim: High Councillor. / Your list ends here. Walk with me — His Majesty’s kingdom keeps better minutes than Surabol.
[68] Kangrim: One question, then we walk. / Were you a righteous traitor, or an unrighteous king?
[69] Bidam: …My father asked me that at a gate. / Write that I was his son. / Tell the sacred country I loved it badly.
[70] ¶ The body finishes falling after the name does.
[71] ¶ Bisamun comes through the lines without a rider, at a walk, and stops over him. Nine beads swing under its jaw. When a Silla groom reaches for the bridle it lays its ears flat and shows him its teeth, and the groom, who has had a long ten days, steps back.
[72] Kim Yushin: Leave it. / …Let it go. North.
[73] ¶ Nobody asks him why north. The horse stands there until the body is taken, then turns and goes, past the Radiance wall and up the valley road, and afterwards the officers on the rampart cannot agree whether anyone opened the gate for it.
[74] [battle]
[75] ¶ Yushin kneels once, only to untie the black headband from the body. Then he stands, mud still wet, turns to the Hwarang behind him and names a house. Bidam’s own line. The one he carried in his jaw and never once claimed aloud.
[76] Kim Yushin: Erase Bidam’s house. / The Son line, every one of them. / Treason’s blood must be cut.
[77] Alchun: Yushin… / Bidam is dead. He poured tea for ten days, then took the blade. / If you burn his hall — we erase one of the Six Elders with our own hands.
[78] ¶ Yushin leans close — close enough that the officers hear only breath, and Alchun hears the sentence.
[79] Kim Yushin: Blood is inevitable…
[80] ¶ Alchun goes pale. Down the line an officer asks for the order to be repeated. Nobody repeats it. Yushin mounts, and the order stands.
[81] ¶ Somewhere behind the palace wall, the queen is already slipping away.
[82] ── SCENE: The Queen’s Bedside ──
[83] ¶ Rain finds the lattice before the physicians do. It is a small rain. It beads on the marshal’s sleeve and on the queen’s mouth, and neither of them has a hand free for it.
[84] Kim Yushin: Your Majesty.
[85] Queen Sunduk: General.
[86] Kim Yushin: The physicians are in the corridor. / I told them the rain can wait.
[87] Queen Sunduk: Leave them. / It is a small rain. It will not be what takes me.
[88] Kim Yushin: Your Majesty—
[89] Queen Sunduk: The year I took the crown. You remember. / You said you would serve me to the end.
[90] Kim Yushin: “I will serve you to the end.”
[91] Queen Sunduk: Yes. / And here we are.
[92] Kim Yushin: Did I not promise to stay to the last moment.
[93] Queen Sunduk: You did. General.
[94] Queen Sunduk: …Princess. / Say it the old way. / When you lost the count on the yard, I was a princess.
[95] Kim Yushin: Hwarang. That is what I was. / A hwarang who lost one count.
[96] Queen Sunduk: You do not lose counts.
[97] Kim Yushin: I lost one. / Which one, I will not say.
[98] Queen Sunduk: Then stop being a general about it.
[99] Queen Sunduk: Dukman.
[100] Kim Yushin: …Don’t.
[101] Queen Sunduk: Since the vote I have been Majesty. / Say the name I had before the room.
[102] Kim Yushin: Dukman.
[103] Queen Sunduk: Yushin.
[104] Kim Yushin: I am here.
[105] Queen Sunduk: I know. / Stay. / I can do a little rain.
[106] ¶ The rain keeps on, small, on the lattice and on his sleeve. Her hand stays in his until it does not. The escort waits until the marshal’s hands have finished their work.
[107] ¶ Kangrim reads her name three times — Dukman. Dukman. Dukman. — the ledger’s habit before a Sacred Bone line closes.
[108] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonders 1 — Queen Seondeok knows three things in advance (善德王知幾三事)): The ministers did not know where that was, and asked, “Where?” The queen said, “South of Mount Nang.” On that very month and day the queen did die, and the ministers buried her on the sunny slope of Mount Nang.❞
[109] ¶ That night Yushin remembers the first morning on the yard, and it is not the way he has been telling it.
[110] ▼ FLASHBACK 610 the twist
    [110.0] ¶ The same desk. The same headband held out across it, still wet at the knuckle end.
    [110.1] Kim Yushin: It’s all right. I will overcome it myself. / My name is Kim Yushin! I will be the great general of Silla!! / Oh — and your name, hyung?
    [110.2] Bidam: My name? Bidam. / That kid…. he’ll be someone great.
[110] ▲ end flashback
[111] ── SCENE: The Empty Pavilion ──
[112] ¶ That night Yushin walks out alone to the pavilion between the old camp lines. The low table is still there, and on it the cup he never touched. He lays the black headband beside it and sits down across from no one.
[113] ▼ FLASHBACK 647 The sixth night · 여섯째 밤
    [113.0] Bidam: **You Gaya wretch…!**
[113] ▲ end flashback
[114] ¶ **The one hand that said no is gone. Now the crown has to fit Seungman, and it was made for someone else…!**
